notes: Written by hand, not by tools/tubuild.py create: at the time of writing, create() raised AttributeError in build_manifest_entry the moment a member of the run had no legacy source, and this run has three such members; it also wrote the .cpp before crashing, so its output could not be trusted as a starting point. That defect has SINCE BEEN FIXED on main (#2315 makes create survive a sourceless member, #2323 makes it emit an // @symbol marker per member), so a future entry for this module need not be hand-written. The builder audited all 301 hand-written rows against the pre-promotion tree: ordinals contiguous 0..300, rows tile 0x020bd828..0x020cfea4 with no gap or overlap, and every legacy_source is both a file in the base tree and an exact-path entry in the base ov002 delinks.txt with the matching extension (173 .cpp, 128 .c).

The source was assembled by a scoped generator that reuses tubuild's own split_legacy_source/unit_functions, because create()'s preamble merge does not scale to 301 members: it emits one merged file-scope declaration per ROM symbol, and 301 independent recoveries of one symbol disagree constantly. Measured instead, and used here: in mwccarm 2004/b56 a declaration written at BLOCK scope inside an `extern "C"` region gets C linkage, and two function bodies may declare one C symbol with different types. So every member keeps its own declarations inside its own body and no call site had to be rewritten to fit a merged spelling. The same is true of DATA declarations -- measured directly, contradicting the earlier belief that block-scope data redeclaration is rejected; only a file-scope redeclaration is. That matters for bytes, not just for tidiness: hoisting one canonical data declaration and casting each member's view back with a macro changed the codegen of six members, and the choice of which spelling became canonical depended on which other members were present.

Only what a function body cannot hold is hoisted: a namespace, a class with static or declared-but-undefined members, and any type named in a member's own signature. Those tags are made unique per member. `struct Sound` and `namespace Sound` were the one true conflict and were resolved to the namespace spelling, which mangles identically.

PRAGMA, measured with the delete-outright control first, and RE-MEASURED by the builder at the shipped revision -- the writer's counts predate the three near-miss recoveries in this branch and no longer reproduce. The shard for ordinal 35, _ZN6Player7SetAnimEji5Fix12IiEj, carries `#pragma opt_propagation off`. Under default deferred codegen that pragma is FILE-GLOBAL: it costs 46 other members their match (255/301 with it file-global, 300/301 with it simply deleted). Bracketing it in #pragma push/pop buys back nothing at all -- also 300/301, byte-identical to deleting it -- because with codegen deferred the state that binds is the state at end of file. `#pragma defer_codegen off` plus a ROM-ASCENDING source order makes the bracket bind positionally and recovers ordinal 35 as well: 301/301, which is what this entry's verification block records. Deleting only `defer_codegen off` still scores 300/301 on bytes, but the emitted .text order reverses (300 out-of-order ordinal pairs) and the pre-link object audit refuses with `licensed .text functions are not emitted in ROM address order`; the byte compare alone would not have caught it. That is why this file is written low address first, the opposite of the default deferred-codegen convention.

Two members needed a source change to survive the C-to-C++ language flip, both the same construct and both from the known scalarization family: a two-int struct copy (`*(Pair2i *)dst = *(Pair2i *)(p + k)`) that C compiles as load/load/store/store and C++ scalarizes into load/store/load/store. The array-wrapper view (`struct P2w { int w[2]; }; *(P2w *)dst = *(P2w *)(p + k);`) restores the ROM's shape exactly, in func_ov002_020c14b8 and func_ov002_020c25a8. Three other spellings were measured and rejected first (two scalar locals: 4 words wrong; copy through a named temporary: 12 bytes too long). The builder diffed all 301 shipped bodies against their pre-promotion shards and found a SECOND change family this note omitted: func_ov002_020c6fe4 and func_ov002_020c897c each do arithmetic on a `void **` load, `*(void**)(c + id*4 + 0xdc) + 0x50`, which is a GNU extension C accepts under -gccext and C++ does not; both casts became `char **`. Byte-neutral -- the address arithmetic is identical -- but an edit. Apart from those four members and the local struct TAG renames that hoisting forces (Vector3 -> Vec3i, V3 -> V3a/V3b, Obj -> ObjHS and Obj2fec, State -> State3i, Camera -> CameraRaw), no body was rewritten.
All 301 members reproduce the cartridge byte-for-byte; none is NONMATCHING and none carries an asm body.

Three members (func_ov002_020d0580, func_ov002_020d06c0, func_ov002_020d2e74) had declared a LOCAL shadow `struct Player`; with the real Player.h type in scope that clashes with their `Player *` parameter, so the shadow was dropped (calls resolve to Player::GetHealth/IsInAir, which mangle to the same ROM symbols) and func_ov002_020d2e74 reads its fields through a file-local `PlayerView` cast. Source changes the fold forced, each measured: (a) func_ov002_020d6dac, func_ov002_020d71ec and func_ov002_020d9dcc first went in as C under `#pragma cplusplus off`, the precedent being func_ov002_020bcdf0, because as C++ they differed by 10, 5 and 29 words. All three now compile as C++ inside extern "C" { }: the two-int struct copies in 020d6dac and 020d71ec go through a single-array wrapper (`struct P2 { int w[2]; }`, as in func_ov002_020c14b8), which restores C's load/load/store/store block copy, and 020d9dcc spells its state test `(int)(x == 0xbf) == 0`, because widening the bool to long long (the C shard's spelling) hoists the early return's 0 ahead of the branch. func_ov002_020bcdf0 is the one C body left. (b) Local shadow types that stood in for the real class were dropped where Player.h is in scope: the `struct State` / `typedef struct State State` stand-ins resolve to Player::State; func_ov002_020df34c and func_ov002_020e2ea0 lose a shadow Player whose IsState/ChangeState calls now bind the real members (same ROM symbols); Player::St_CrazedCrate_Cleanup loses its field-view Player, and its write of the byte at 0x6e1 is spelled mJumpComboStage. Block-scope declarations of names that Player.h already declares as class members are dropped from Player:: member bodies; func_ov002_020d85fc calls Player::TryGrab as a member, and func_ov002_020d06c0, Player::St_SideFlip_Main and Player::Behavior call Player::IsState as a member (byte-identical; once IsState is defined in this file, a mangled call that opens a source line reads as a hand-spelled definition to tools/langmode_audit.py). (c) include/Player.h gains the missing declaration `int St_CrazedCrate_Cleanup();`, which the shard had supplied through its shadow class; adding a non-virtual member declaration changes no consumer's layout. (d) C spellings C++ rejects: a parameter named `this` (func_ov002_020d4d88) became `self`; two `char *c = self;` gained a cast (func_ov002_020d8360); func_ov002_020d4c30 drops its shadow `struct Sound` (Sound.h is included) and an unused shadow `Particle::System`, and its extern "C" NewSimple declaration leaves the `Particle` namespace it sat in, so the call names the ROM symbol directly; func_ov002_020e2c84 gained the prototype its shard used implicitly; Player::St_Fly_Main's extern prototypes lost parameter names its body's `#define c` would rewrite; the `enum { false, true };` stand-ins were dropped. (e) Types with a user destructor are hoisted to file scope with TU-unique names (PVec, PVec869c, PVec8944, Vector3e968) so their vague-linkage D1s are licensed by compiler_only_output rows; the remaining local shadow structs keep C linkage under unique tags. Player::InitResources keeps the inline asm block its shard carried. Baselines: the member definitions sit inside `extern "C" { }`, which tools/check_decl_agreement.py does not index, so retiring a shard removes its declarations from that gate's plurality vote; the resulting flips are banked in config/decl-agreement-baseline.json.
